items.statement: Let E be a finite-dimensional real Hilbert space equipped with its Borel measurable structure, including rank zero. Let μ be any probability measure, η>0, and f:E→ℝ a globally C1 function with compact support. For every y∈E define R_y=μ.tilted(x↦−‖x−y‖²/(2η)) and S_y=(x↦2x−y)_#R_y. Then the exact function m(y)=∫f(u)S_y(du) is globally C1. These are the specified everywhere-defined posterior and reflection laws; no arbitrary AE conditional version is substituted. Moment, input density, domination, normalization, derivative-continuity and closed-gradient certificates are not premises. This is explicitly attributed authored analytic background for the paper’s normalized-density differentiation with its Gibbs input and smooth compact tests.
assumptions: Finite-dimensional real Hilbert/Borel space E; rank zero included as an explicit authored extension.
Any actual probability measure μ, any η>0 and any globally C1 real observer f with compact support; no centering or finite-moment/input-density premise.
R_y and S_y are exactly the displayed quadratic tilt and affine reflected pushforward at every y. The source-volume Gibbs density identity is a separate downstream adapter.
All observer/derivative bounds, measurability, genuine L1, dominated differentiation, continuous integrated derivative and positive normalization are internal outputs, not convenience binders.
